title: Bunny Companion presentation state
description: Everything a companion user interface is permitted to know, projected from the canonical event stream in schemas/companion-core-event.schema.json. This is a *presentation* schema and carries no authority: nothing here is stored, nothing is replayed from it, and a client cannot cause anything by sending one. It exists so that the surface can be rebuilt from the record rather than from a parallel copy of it, and so that what the surface may contain is a list somebody can read. The absent fields are the specification: there is no property here for hidden model reasoning, an API credential, a provider token, a raw or unredacted tool result, a screen capture, a microphone sample, or an arbitrary internal object, and adding one would require changing this file. Every string that reaches a screen has been through companion.privacy.display_summary at the "ui" audience ceiling, whose maximum classification is "sensitive": a "secret" task's contents arrive as a withheld marker with contentWithheld set.

phase.description: What the surface shows, after priority resolution. Where several are true at once the order in companion.presentation.PHASE_PRIORITY decides, so an unanswered approval outranks work in progress and an error outranks everything. "disconnected" is produced only by a client that cannot reach the runtime; the runtime never emits it.

basePhase.description: What the event stream alone produced, before priority. Kept so a client can explain what it is showing and a test can tell a mapping fault from a priority fault.

statusText.description: A deterministic sentence derived from the event type and its sanitized payload. Never a model's words and never free-form provider output.

progress.description: Monotonic. A fraction that retreated would tell the user the machine had lost track, which the record does not say.

disagreement.description: True for an observation the runtime recorded as a material disagreement. Separate from severity so that a client does not have to re-derive the threshold, and so a disagreement stays visible after the executor revises around it.

absent.description: The reviewer produced nothing. Silence is never assent.

approvalState.description: How the current question ended. 'withdrawn' means the system took the question back — because the task was paused, cancelled, or the plan was superseded — and is deliberately distinct from 'denied', which means a person refused. A surface that showed 'denied' for a withdrawal would tell somebody they had refused something they never saw.

approvals.description: Open questions. Every field an answer must repeat back is here; the runtime checks all of them against the request it recorded before a decision is accepted.

destination.description: The binding destination, in the approval layer's vocabulary. This is the value the runtime recorded and therefore the value an answer must repeat.

destinationDetail.description: The specific place, for the person reading the dialog. Display only, and deliberately outside the binding: it is a rendering, not a record.

expiresAtMonotonic.description: Shown so the user can see the question will lapse. Not part of the binding an answer repeats: the runtime checks expiry against its own record, because a client-supplied expiry is the one field an attacker would want to restate.

safeDefault.description: What happens if nobody answers. Always a denial for a sensitive action; there is no configuration that makes it a grant.

prompt.description: The structured facts a permission surface draws. Display only, and outside the binding for the same reason destinationDetail is: it is a rendering, not a record, and binding a rendering would mean rewording a sentence invalidates an answer somebody already gave. Every field is an allowlisted key bounded by companion.presentation.PROMPT_FIELDS, because several of these strings originate in an application's own manifest and they are being drawn in a security dialog.

listening.description: A microphone is on. Set by the client, never by the runtime: audio never becomes an event.

implementation.description: What will actually be drawn. Restricted to what this build implements. animated-2d joined when companion.character.animated_renderer existed; full-3d and lightweight-3d joined when companion.character.three_d.renderer existed and a test drew a frame with it and read the pixels back. A value only joins this list when a renderer is behind it, which is why it was shorter than eligiblePresentation for two phases.

eligible.description: What the machine and the capability policy would permit. May name something this build cannot draw — saying so is the honest form of "eligible" and is why it is a separate field.

captions.description: Captions are produced in every presentation, including audio-only. They are the authoritative rendering of what the companion said; audio is the optional one.

explanationReference.description: Which part of the record explains the current decision — a capability plan id, or a plan the approval was raised against. A reference, not an explanation: the explanation is in the event stream.

revision.description: The event sequence this state was folded up to. A client sends it back as afterSequence and is given only what it has not seen.

contentWithheld.description: Something the projection read was above the "ui" ceiling and arrived as a marker. A surface showing a redacted view should say so rather than look complete.
